Subject: Residency pin orchestration & logging controls — CardioData follow-up

Hi Marta / Tom —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from our side and the concrete items we promised to follow up on: 

Summary (from call)
- Primary ask: CardioData wants production inference traffic pinned to a single US region (us-east-1) with a cross-region failover plan to eu-west-1 only for disaster recovery.
- PII scope: request to ensure user-identifying PII (name, email, national id) is never replicated outside the pinned region except for encrypted backups and support traces under explicit controls.
- Logging: audit logs (auth events, admin activity) can be exported to your analytics stack; request is for logs to be retained 12 months by default, with an option to redact query-level content.

Deliverables we promised:
1) Short ops checklist describing: pinning configuration, cross-region failover triggers, backup replication policy and encryption-at-rest/transport.
2) Table of where different data classes live (PII, non-PII, model KV cache, request/response logs) and whether they cross region boundaries.
3) SOC2/Risk artefacts and a pointer to our logging redaction options.

Ask for you:
- Confirm that the pinned region should be us-east-1 (you mentioned preference for US East) — reply with any objections.
- Confirm retention target for raw request/response logs: 90 days (default) vs 12 months (requested by your security team).
- Let us know if you require backups to be held in a separate geo (e.g., long-term snapshots kept in eu-west-1) or if single-region backups are acceptable.

Next steps / timeline
- Today: send ops checklist + SOC2 summary (attached).
- Early next week (Mon/Tue): proposed technical follow-up with our infra engineer (Alex) to walk the pinning config and RPO/RTO numbers.
- By next Wed: updated contract language around data residency and backup scope for procurement.

Attachments: redwood-residency-ops-checklist.pdf (ops checklist), SOC2-summary-2027.pdf (summary)

Happy to jump on a quick call to walk the checklist. Proposed time: Monday 10:00–11:00 ET.

Best,
Soojin

Thanks, Soojin — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side before we lock times: 

Quick questions:
1) Can you provide a simple matrix that says, for each artifact (user profile PII, embeddings, logs, backups), whether it is:
   - stored only in pinned region,
   - replicated as encrypted snapshot to backup region, or
   - streamed to external analytics (we need to know if anything leaves us-east-1 in plaintext)

2) For cross-region failover: what is the default RTO/RPO if you trigger failover to eu-west-1? We need numbers (seconds/minutes/hours).

3) Logging redaction: we need to confirm whether request/response bodies can be redacted at ingestion and whether redaction prevents content from being stored in S3/long-term logs.

4) Backups: we prefer backups to remain in US for now, but security may ask to keep a long-term encrypted snapshot in eu-west-1 for compliance later — can you outline how that would be handled and how keys would be managed?

We asked security to join the thread (cc). Also, can you send the ops checklist as a table (not PDF) so our security team can comment inline?

Thanks — Marta

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Residency pin orchestration & logging controls — internal answers / draft table

Internal — drafting the concrete table and proposed defaults to send back to CardioData. Please review and flag anything we should change before reply-all.

Proposed data-location matrix (defaults)
- User profile PII: stored encrypted in us-east-1 only. Not replicated. (Customer-managed KMS key option available.)
- Embeddings / model KV cache: stored in us-east-1; cache snapshots for warm standby can be replicated to eu-west-1 but snapshots are encrypted and access-controlled. Replication only on DR enablement.
- Request/response logs: retained in us-east-1 by default. Can stream metadata (timestamps, latency, status codes) to your analytics (external) over TLS; request/response payloads are redacted on ingestion unless customer opts in for full capture.
- Backups / snapshots: daily encrypted snapshots retained 30 days in us-east-1. Long-term snapshots (90+ days) can be copied to eu-west-1 on request; copies are encrypted with a separate key and gated behind an approval workflow (procurement/security signoff).

Failover RTO/RPO (defaults)
- RPO: 15 minutes for in-memory/kv caches (best effort) if warm standby enabled; 24 hours for full snapshot restore if standby not configured.
- RTO: with warm standby and auto-failover policies: 5–15 minutes to start serving in eu-west-1 (depending on session recovery). Without warm standby: 2–6 hours for restore from snapshot and model load.

Logging redaction behavior
- Redaction at ingestion will strip request/response bodies from long-term logs; metadata remains (IDs, timestamps, latency). Redaction prevents payloads from being written to long-term S3 logs and downstream analytics exports.

Key management
- Customer-managed KMS supported. If CardioData wants copies in eu-west-1, we recommend separate regional keys; cross-region key replication is possible but requires policy alignment and audit.

Attachments to send to customer: exported table (CSV) and the ops checklist as a Google Doc for inline comments.

Action items for internal team:
- Ben: please review the RTO/RPO wording and confirm numbers can be guaranteed under Dedicated vs Hosted modes.
- Monica: prepare a Google Doc version of the checklist and share with CardioData security.

I'll wait for your quick thumbs — planning to reply to Marta with the table and answers tomorrow morning.

Alex

Marta / Tom / Security team —

Thanks for the clarifying questions. See answers below (inline) and the attached Google Doc link for the ops checklist so your security team can comment directly: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cCardioData-Residency

Inline answers
Q1: matrix of artifacts -> see table below (also attached as CSV)
- User profile PII: stored only in us-east-1 (no replication by default). Customer-managed KMS supported; we can enforce region-bound keys.
- Embeddings / cache: primary in us-east-1. Warm-standby replication to eu-west-1 is possible; we will only replicate encrypted snapshots and only if DR is enabled by the customer.
- Request/response logs: metadata can be streamed; payloads are redacted on ingestion by default. If you require full payload capture, that is an opt-in and would be stored only in us-east-1 unless long-term snapshot copy to eu-west-1 is requested.
- Backups: daily encrypted snapshots retained 30 days in us-east-1. Long-term copies (90+ days) to eu-west-1 possible with separate KMS and approval workflow.

Q2: RTO/RPO -> numbers (defaults)
- Warm standby enabled: RPO ≈ 15 minutes (kv sync), RTO ≈ 5–15 minutes (service warm-up and KV restore).
- Standby disabled: RPO ≈ 24 hours (daily snapshot), RTO ≈ 2–6 hours (snapshot restore + model load).

Q3: Logging redaction -> behavior
- Redaction at ingestion removes payload content from long-term storage and prevents export to downstream analytics. We retain metadata (IDs, timestamps, error codes). If you need redaction rules (PII patterns), Alex will share the current regex/table.

Q4: Backups and key management
- We support customer-managed keys. For cross-region copies we recommend a separate regional CMK in eu-west-1; copies are encrypted with that key and access is restricted to a small set of ops principals and gated by a change request.

Attached: ops-checklist (Google Doc link above) and CSV export of the table. Also attached: SOC2-summary-2027.pdf for your security review.

Proposed next step: technical walkthrough with Alex on Monday 10:00 AM ET (same as proposed). Send a calendar invite and we’ll include a short demo of the pinning UI and the failover policy toggle.

If Security prefers, we can pause on any eu-west-1 copy until an internal review is complete.

Thanks — and looking forward to the call.

Soojin
